- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and prices are trending down, model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; allow slight lagged rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next period — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — apply small upward bias (0.5–1.5%) for short-term forecasts.  
- In multi-day forecasts (e.g., 10+ days), model shows mean reversion bias — if recent 5-day average is rising, forecast should not drop below 10% below that average.  
- When sentiment is neutral (±0.05) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much — allow 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast.
